cards.text: Jesus just called out the Pharisees and the experts in the law at a dinner, and now they're bitterly opposing Him, waiting to catch Him in something He says (Luke 11:53-54). Meanwhile, a crowd of many thousands has packed in so tight they're trampling one another. That's not a crowd, friend. That's a doorbuster sale at 5 a.m.

cards.question: True or false: With thousands pressing in, Jesus starts by speaking to His disciples.

cards.text: His first words are a warning: beware of "the leaven of the Pharisees." And remember, Jesus just told the Pharisees they clean the outside of the cup while the inside is full of greed and wickedness (Luke 11:39).

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples what the leaven of the Pharisees is. What does He call it?

cards.text: Then Jesus says there's nothing concealed that won't be disclosed, and nothing hidden that won't be made known. That's every private group chat that EVER got screenshotted, friend.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says what the disciples have spoken in the dark will stay in the dark.
Jesus says what the disciples have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the ___.

cards.text: Next, Jesus calls the disciples "My friends." He tells them not to be afraid of those who kill the body.

cards.question: Jesus tells His friends not to fear the people who can kill the body. What's His reason?

answers.text: After that they can do no more
They will never catch the disciples
The crowd will stand up for them

cards.question: So if not them, who does Jesus say the disciples should fear?

answers.text: The One with authority to throw them into hell
The Pharisees who are watching Him closely
The rulers who can drag them into court

cards.text: Then Jesus points to sparrows: five of them sell for two pennies. Friend, I came out of a closing-day bin with a 25-cent sticker on me, and even I'm saying that's CHEAP.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says sparrows are so cheap that God forgets some of them.

cards.text: Then Jesus says even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. I can't keep count of my own mustache, friend, and I use it as HANDS.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples not to be afraid, because they are worth more than many ___.

cards.text: Now Jesus talks about confessing Him before men, owning up to Him in front of people. Not a quiet little thumbs-up in the group chat, friend.

cards.question: When someone confesses Jesus before men, what does Jesus say the Son of Man will do?

answers.text: Confess him before the angels of God
Reward him in front of the crowds
Make him a ruler over Israel

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says whoever denies Him before men will be denied before the angels of God.

cards.text: Then Jesus gets serious. Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven.

cards.question: But Jesus says one kind of blasphemy will not be forgiven. Blasphemy against whom?

cards.text: Last, Jesus says the disciples will be brought before synagogues, rulers and authorities. Me? I'd be up all night practicing my speech in the bathroom mirror.

cards.question: When the disciples are brought before rulers and authorities, what does Jesus tell them not to worry about?

answers.text: How long they will be held

cards.question: Jesus says that at that time the ___ will teach the disciples what they should say.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Jesus has thousands of people listening, and trust me, He's not done teaching yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "the leaven of the Pharisees.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: the Luke 11:53-54 context, the trampling crowd, "That's not a crowd, friend." and "That's a doorbuster sale at 5 a.m." The limit is three.

rule.text: **The opening card** can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The card says the Pharisees "clean the outside of the cup while the inside is full of greed and wickedness," which puts the greed and wickedness inside the cup. Luke 11:39 says the Pharisees themselves are full of greed and wickedness inside ("but inside you are full of greed and wickedness").

rule.text: **Retelling:** Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Story card 5 already tells Luke 12:2: nothing concealed won't be disclosed and nothing hidden won't be made known. That gives away the answer to this card, which asks whether what is spoken in the dark will stay in the dark. Card 5 is a story card, not an answered choice card, so this isn't a permitted follow-up.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. Once a choice has been answered, the cards after it can build on that answer.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word that finishes Jesus's line ("proclaimed from the ___": housetops, city gates or temple courts). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason out "housetops" over the other two. It tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

findings.problem: The card cites Luke 12:12 but tells nothing from that verse. Its only passage fact, the thousands of people listening, comes from Luke 12:1.

rule.text: **Cite exactly what the card uses.** Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The closing line closely copies the doc's example ("And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done."). It uses the same opening structure and the same "trust me" turn.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
